summary: Minimal but correct T1 — one UDP query, deterministic disclosure. Only emits a single finding kind. Biggest gap is aggregation and downstream chaining: hostname/domain/DC-role should feed into SMB/LDAP/kerb modules, and MAC OUI should feed device-type fingerprinting. The is_dc flag is captured but not surfaced as its own finding (DC-role discovery on 137/udp is a strong recon signal).

findings.title_pattern: NetBIOS Name Service discloses hostname / workgroup / MAC
findings.tier_evidence: NBNS node-status query answered with name list + MAC — deterministic wire evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: Split into 3 kinds: netbios_dc_discovery (is_dc=true, medium severity — high-value recon), netbios_mac_oui (add OUI vendor lookup — device-type identification), and the base disclosure. Auto-ingest hostname->IP and workgroup/domain into shared surfaces for SMB/LDAP/kerb pivot.
findings.tester_next_step: nbtscan -v <ip>; then use disclosed hostname: rpcclient -U '' -N <ip>; if suffix 0x1C present: kerbrute userenum -d <domain> --dc <ip> users.txt.
